DWTNeRF bypasses this by decomposing the image into frequency sub-bands [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that DWTNeRF decomposes the rendered view and ground-truth view into four sub-bands (LL, LH, HL, HH) using the Discrete Wavelet Transform. It further clarifies that this approach is used instead of frequency masking because INGP's hash encoding does not strictly map inputs to high frequencies, effectively bypassing the limitations of previous methods by handling frequency sub-bands directly.

The claim states that the method introduces a Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) loss to prioritize low-frequency learning and uses multi-head attention for cross-branch interactions without changing the base MLP architecture, which avoids performance degradation in Instant-NGP.
